taxonomyNote: NatureServe lists the primary name 'Variable Groundsnake' and follows Cox et al. (2018), which split the former S. semiannulata into S. semiannulata, S. episcopa, S. taylori and S. mosaueri; Wikipedia's wider range (including Colorado, Kansas, Missouri and Oklahoma) reflects the older, broader concept.
fieldMarks: Small snake, total length about 8-19 in (20-48 cm), with smooth dorsal scales, a small head and a round pupil.
Colour and pattern vary widely even within one area: brown, red or orange with black banding, orange or brown striping, or solid-coloured.
Underside is typically white or gray.
The head marking is said to suggest a bishop's miter, the origin of the name 'miter snake'.
behavior: Secretive and mostly nocturnal, sometimes abroad at dusk; often found on roadsides or in dry drainage ditches at night.
Active from spring to late summer; active as early as mid-March in west Texas.
Eats spiders, scorpions, centipedes, crickets, grasshoppers and insect larvae.
Shelters under rocks and other cover or burrows in fine windblown sand at the base of bushes or grass hummocks; lays 3-6 eggs, usually June-July.
habitat: Arid and semiarid country: river bottoms, desert flats, sand hummocks and rocky hillsides with pockets of loose soil, from prairie and desert lowlands to pinyon-juniper and oak-pine zones; in California it favours areas with fine wind-blown sand, up to about 1,400 m.
range: Southwestern United States and northern Mexico: southeastern Oregon, southwestern Idaho, eastern California, western Nevada, southwestern Utah, western and southern Arizona, southwestern New Mexico and extreme western Texas. Not in Canada.
